newsitem.title: CHINA: Low prices trim Shanghai Petro profit.
newsitem.headline: Low prices trim Shanghai Petro profit.

text.p: Shanghai Petrochemical Co Ltd, which reported a 52.6 percent plunge in net profits for 1996, said on Tuesday it was being hit by falling prices for its products and rising raw material costs.
"In 1996, the petrochemical market had a correction with prices of petrochemical products dropping sharply," the company's annual report, published on Tuesday, said.
"In addition, crude prices rose sharply. This faced the company with a stiff challenge," it added.

The company's annual results, issued on Monday, showed a 52.6 percent fall in net profits in 1996 to a billion yuan from 2.1 billion yuan in 1995 under international accounting standards. Turnover rose to 12.2 billion yuan from 12.06 billion yuan.
Shanghai stock analysts said the results had been expected and would have little likely impact on the share price, listed in both Hong Kong and on the domestic board of the Shanghai stock exchange.
Trading in the shares was suspended on Tuesday morning on publication of the annual report and will resume in the afternoon.
"The poor results had been expected by the market following the firm's weak performance in the first half of 1996," said one analyst.
"We had forecasted a profit fall of around 45 percent, so this is not a surprise," said an analyst with a foreign brokerage in Shanghai.
